title.narrative: Institute of Economic and Social Studies (IESE) 2023-2025
Institute of Economic and Social Studies (IESE) 2023-2025

description.narrative: Founded in 2007, IESE is now the main player in independent research in Mozambique in economics, sociology and political science. They contribute to the strengthening of knowledge, intellectual capacity and information to the public debate. IESE is applying for support from Sweden with the following objectives (quoted from IESE Strategic Plan 2015-2025): (i) Enhance the capacity of IESE researchers through training and its completion; and ii) Ensure IESE's overall goal of creating a better and more equitable society, with inclusive growth and greater political participation, in line with Mozambique's international development commitments, including several UN Development Goals; iii) Implement the final phase of the IESE Strategic Plan 2016-2025, which has three specific objectives: (a) Consolidate and deepen research; b) Enhance research through social and academic intervention; and c) Ensure institutional development and sustainability. Since its inception, IESE has been funded through a joint fund (in Sida terminology, core support) with various donors - Finland, Sweden, Switzerland, Ireland, Denmark and Norway. However, since 2015, contributions to the Common Fund have decreased. Sweden's civil society support AGIR ended in 2020 and with it our funding to IESE, which was channelled through Oxfam Ibis.

IESE grundades 2007 och är nu huvudaktör inom oberoende forskning i Moçambique i ekonomi, sociologi och statsvetenskap. De bidrar till stärkt kunskap, intellektuell kapacitet och med information till den offentliga debatten. IESE ansöker om stöd från Sverige med följande mål (citerat från IESE Strategic Plan 2015-2025): i) Förbättra IESE:s forskares kapacitet genom utbildning och slutförande av denna; och ii) Garantera IESE:s övergripande mål att skapa ett bättre och rättvisare samhälle, med inkluderande tillväxt och större politiskt deltagande, i linje med Moçambiques internationella utvecklingsåtaganden, inklusive flera FN:s utvecklingsmål; iii) Implementera den sista fasen av IESE:s strategiska plan 2016-2025, som har tre specifika mål: a) Konsolidera och fördjupa forskningen; b) Förbättra forskning genom social och akademisk intervention; och c) Säkerställa institutionell utveckling och hållbarhet IESE har sedan det grundades finansierats genom en gemensam fond (i Sida-terminologi, kärnstöd) med olika givare - Finland, Sverige, Schweiz, Irland, Danmark och Norge. Sedan 2015 har dock bidragen till gemensamma fonden minskat. Sveriges civilsamhällestöd AGIR avslutades 2020 och därmed även vår finansiering till IESE, som kanaliserades via Oxfam Ibis.

The core support to IESE 2023 - 2026 has the following objectives:
i) Improve the capacity of IESE researchers through training and skills upgrading
ii) Guarantee IESE's overall goal of creating a better and fairer society, with inclusive growth and greater political participation, in line with Mozambique's international development commitments, including several UN development goals;
iii) Implement the final years of IESE's strategic plan 2016-2025, which has three specific objectives:
a) Consolidate and deepen research; b) Improving research through social and academic intervention; and c) Ensure institutional development and sustainability
In addition to the core support, Sida is also supporting IESE's work on their Social cohesion barometer (SCB), which has the main purpose of describing, analysing and understanding the dynamics of social cohesion between state and citizens as well as between citizens and groups in the districts concerned. The SCB is also intended to provide systematic information on the situation in the affected districts and develop the capacity of local stakeholders and authorities to promote a peaceful society, maintain governance and better service delivery at the district level such as inclusive development plans and budgets at the municipal, district and provincial levels.

description.narrative:
IESE's 2025 interventions contributed to stronger evidence-informed dialogue on governance, social cohesion, and development challenges in Mozambique. Research findings were used by national dialogue actors, local governments, civil society organizations, and development partners. The programme strengthened the capacity of stakeholders to analyse, discuss, and respond to social cohesion and governance challenges, while also contributing to the creation of new accountability and coordination mechanisms. Particularly significant was the use of Social Cohesion Barometer findings in national reform discussions and the establishment of a Civil Society Organisations Forum for Social Accountability.
Expected results were largely achieved in relation to research production, dissemination, policy engagement and institutional strengthening. Particularly noteworthy was the successful expansion of the Social Cohesion Barometer and the use of research findings in the National Inclusive Dialogue process. Unexpected results included the creation of a civil society accountability platform and strengthened collaboration with child rights organisations. At the same time, implementation was constrained by staffing shortages, resource limitations and delays in dissemination and publication activities. Several outputs were postponed rather than cancelled, suggesting a need to strengthen results planning, risk management and adaptive management processes. In this context, consideration could be given to a targeted RBM and Adaptive Management support assignment to strengthen outcome tracking, articulation of policy influence results, and management of implementation risks.
The results presented here contribute to Strategic Goal 2.1: strengthening democracy and respect for human rights and the rule of law, including the reduction of corruption and 4.1 Strengthening the conditions for preventing and managing crises and conflicts peacefully. The results presented are included in the 2025 annual report IESE. Annual report 2025, Klaradia UM2022/27701/MAPU-85.
Expected Result 1: Strengthened research capacity of IESE researchers (Page 13). IESE successfully strengthened the research capacity of its staff through six methodological seminars covering topics such as elections, microhistory, natural disasters and education, youth resilience, and academic writing. In addition, four training sessions on artificial intelligence for research, documentation, and communication were completed, achieving full implementation of these planned capacity-building activities.
Expected Result 2: Research conducted on topics relevant to society (Pages 1416). IESE achieved significant progress in conducting research relevant to Mozambican society. The institute completed seven Social Cohesion Barometers in northern Mozambique, three political economy analyses, two district case studies, one study on women, violence and memory, one gender dynamics study, and two conflict sensitivity analyses. It also completed research projects on finance and development, economic resilience in conflict areas, social protection and climate change, and development cooperation dynamics.
IESE actively participated in Mozambique's National Inclusive Dialogue, primarily by contributing research evidence rather than directly participating in political negotiations. The report states that IESE maintained contact with the Dialogue's technical committee, presented findings from its Social Cohesion Barometer in two closed meetings organised by the committee, and made two additional presentations at civil society events supporting the dialogue. IESE's contribution focused on informing discussions around governance, social cohesion, civic space, and citizens' perceptions of public institutions. (pp. 45)
However, the report does not provide evidence that IESE directly influenced or secured the adoption of specific reforms emerging from the Inclusive Dialogue. Rather than claiming policy change, the report documents activities such as presenting research, engaging policymakers, disseminating evidence, and supporting national debate. These are important policy engagement outputs, but they do not demonstrate that IESE's recommendations were incorporated into legislation or institutional reforms. (pp. 47)
Expected Result 3: Effective dissemination of research findings (Pages 1718). IESE successfully disseminated research results through conferences, workshops, and provincial seminars. The 7th IESE International Conference, and two Social Cohesion International Conferences. The institute also produced new communication products, including two infographics and three videos on social cohesion, while maintaining active engagement with media and public audiences.
Expected Result 4: Strengthened social intervention and stakeholder engagement (Page 19). IESE enhanced the use of research findings by distributing publications nationwide, developing a curriculum for civil servant training on social cohesion, facilitating public debates, and establishing a new partnership with the Civil Society Forum for Child Rights in Mozambique (ROSC). These activities strengthened links between research, policy dialogue, and community-level interventions.
Unexpected Result
Expansion of the Social Cohesion Barometer despite USAID withdrawal (Page 5). Although the closure of USAID created uncertainty in Mozambiques development sector, IESE was able to extend the Social Cohesion Barometer survey to the districts of Balama, Meconta, and Nacala-a-Velha. This expansion occurred despite the loss of anticipated USAID involvement, demonstrating resilience and continuity of the programme.
Creation of the Civil Society Organisations Forum for Social Accountability (Page 8).. During the Just Transition Learning Project workshop, participants established a new mechanism known as the Civil Society Organisations Forum for Social Accountability. This forum was not highlighted as a planned outcome but emerged from stakeholder engagement and aims to promote dialogue and accountability regarding mining and energy projects, providing a platform for future advocacy and policy influence.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
